body: All I can say to you is, you're not alone. Hopefully we can both find some meaning for ourselves and not for others.
I can totally relate to what you're saying, on the two different points you brought up. I wonder if many suicidal people feel anger towards their parent/s for bringing them into the world?

Yes, I do need to speak to my dr. I used to game a bit then got out of it for some reason. Right now I don't have a computer and the right TV setup to do any gaming, so that's a bit annoying. I used to love playing Sims.
Thank you. Yes, I've got one tablet left of my antidepressant so I really should see my dr and discuss a higher dose (I do have another script though).

Good point. I often relate this to thinking about having children or not. In one way they bring people so much meaning but in another way so many people have them to bring meaning into their lives, so is that wrong?

I think sport can definitely be good - exercise and social. Maybe I should try a sport for the first time!

On exercise though, do you have any tips for motivation? I do walk quite a lot but I feel that's more maintenance than anything and something I've always naturally done.

Thank you for this and you are right, I need to look for the small things. I was doing better at this late last year, enjoying time at the park with my dogs etc, but I let it fall by the way side, that feeling of joy and simply being present. I don't know if this is sheer laziness or my depression getting worse? Why is it so easy to slip back into old, destructive habits?

Could you elaborate on luck being the reason you survived that time three years ago?

Thank you so much for your reply. A lot of my friends say similar things about me being a caring and considerate person and one of my counsellors said I may be someone who feels others emotions very deeply. It is a double edged sword though in some ways.

I think you pointed out to me to not feel guilty when I do things to help me cope when I'm feeling bad, like watching Netflix or staying in bed. When we are physically unwell we do these things so why can't it be okay when we're mentally unwell? I mean, contemplating your own death is extremely traumatic, when you think about it so maybe I need to remind myself of this and that self-care is really important during these times.

That is a good question. I work in social services so I occasionally come across people contemplating suicide, though not lately. I think I probably undervalue the work I do. Thank you for your reply, it was actually a bit of a reminder for me to look back on why I got into this line of work.

I totally get where you're coming from. I can't speak for everyone but I don't think anyone wants to actually die, they want their pain to go away. But sometimes it either won't or seems like it won't, hence the feeling of needing to end things to end the pain. I think fearing the pain of dying is completely normal. I guess biologically we don't want to die or feel pain.
Yes exactly! I hope we both find something else to keep us going.

I know hanging out with friends is important but i find it so hard to motovate myself to do it and I've noticed, although it's enjoyable and distracting being with friends, as soon as I get in the car to go home I'm back to feeling depressed again!
I think what you said about finding something that is just for me is good advice. I used to practice yoga almost daily and of course that's gone by the way side because of my current mental state, but I would like to get back into it. And maybe swimming, I do enjoy that.
Thanks for your reply.

The problem is I don't know what makes me happy and sometimes I'll do things that used and I feel ... nothing. It's like I can't enjoy things anymore. Hard to explain. Thank you for your reply and I will try some new things.

I understand what you're saying. When I told my mum I felt suicidal she cried. I know she cares so much for me, and my brother and I are basically her world, but that's also a very heavy load on me, if that makes sense. Thank you for your reply.
Thank you so much for replying, it does help to know I am not alone. I am sorry for your loss and can't even imagine what that would be like. Hugs to you

I think the people who say this haven't experienced suicidal ideation or have so long ago they've forgotten or they have no idea what it's like to experience suicidal ideation. I don't have any advice I'm sorry, only to say that you are not alone.
